reply_text:
The slow part is one rule: secret-like keywords (`password = …`), at 2.3 s of the 3.5 s per 8 MB. Checking whether a cheap exact prefilter is possible.Now the builder that joins everything into one file. It includes the full source of each piece rather than code hidden in strings, so a cautious reader can see what it does.It timed out after 5 minutes, even limited to the last hour. Checking how much log data that hour actually covers.No uncommitted edits, so I'll change only how the keyword rule searches, not what it matches. Then I'll check the old and new versions give identical findings on real logs, and run claude-3's tests.Findings are identical on all 12 edge cases and on 10,000 real log lines (232 findings), and it runs 2.3 times faster. claude-3's tests pass. Timing a whole large file again.All tests pass. In the Codex logs the relayed turns are marked `Origin: unknown`, so they're now skipped. Rerunning on the same half hour of real logs.Gist: The single file is built, and the staging home page now has a click-to-copy box under "solve the problems you want solved": a two-line download-and-run command, a direct download link, and the file's checksum. You can see it at zone.hyperreal.enterprises/staging/. Nothing is public until you push. One thing to know first: on your own logs it's slow, about 100 seconds for half an hour of activity, because you run so many agents. Most people's logs are far smaller.

**What the file does** (`xiaoxiang-local.py`, 192 KB, standard library only, no network)
- **Reads your logs:** everything in `~/.claude/projects` and `~/.codex/sessions`, or only recent logs with `--days N`.
- **Finds the turns you typed.** It skips:
  - tool results;
  - subagent traffic;
  - text the tools inject (environment context, AGENTS.md, slash-command wrappers);
  - agent-to-agent bells.
- **Classifies after redacting:** it removes secrets from each turn first, then classifies it with 小象.
- **Counts suspected credentials** by distinct value as well as total occurrences.
- **Prints only counts, kinds and file paths.** It never prints turn text or secret values.

**What your last half hour showed, and what I changed because of it**
- **Turns:** at first it counted 2,573 turns as typed by you. Most were bells between agents, which Codex stores as user messages. Relayed turns now count only if they're marked as coming from the operator, which leaves 53.
- **Credentials:** it first reported 47,595. They were mostly Agency receipt tokens repeated inside Codex's compacted history, so it now also reports 1,781 distinct values.
- **The named keys** (Anthropic, AWS, GitHub…) are almost all the fake keys from the scanner's own test files, logged by the sessions that wrote those tests. I checked the remaining six by length and position, without printing any values: they're stubs or false positives, not real keys.

**Speed-up to `secret_scan.py`** (f1dc0b12). One rule, the keyword one (`password = …`), was retrying at every character, so long runs of base64 in the logs made it very slow. It now looks only where a keyword actually appears. Findings are identical on 12 edge cases and 10,000 real log lines, and claude-3's tests pass. It runs at 3.6 MB/s, up from 1.8. I checked there were no uncommitted edits before changing their file.

**Two scanner gaps to pass to claude-3:**
- "the password is: X" isn't caught, because of the "is" between the keyword and the colon;
- the url-credentials rule matches across escaped quotes.

**Tests:** 5 new ones, all passing. One runs the single file on its own, in a temporary folder with a made-up home directory and a planted secret. It checks the counts, and that neither the secret nor any turn text appears in the output.

**Before publishing**, two things to decide:
- **Keep it separate:** the box sits in the draft home page, so it would go live with whatever else is in the draft.
- **Your words ship in the file:** the embedded model is built from your labelled turns, filtered the same way as the 小象 page. Please look at the draft page before pushing.

**Commits:** futon3c f1dc0b12 and 0af3002d; futon7 8b92e48.
